ceiling_directive: Prove rational positive-separator existence with an effective height bound for the declared exact-CI chambers, thereby replacing generic real-algebraic feasibility witnesses with bounded rational certificates.
improvement_directive: Resolve `oeq:effect-complete-rational-atlas` by proving that feasibility of the effect-separation formula on these exact-CI chambers implies a strictly positive rational separator, with an effective input-dependent height bound. Instantiate the construction on a nontrivial tied-family example.
critique: The main completeness theorem establishes decidability through exhaustive DAG enumeration and generic real-closed-field quantifier elimination, but supplies no degree, height, certificate-length, or usable runtime bound, so it does not yet justify the proposed operational use in Tetrad or GSP. The sole worked cross-MEC example produces an ambiguity certificate rather than a common effect missed by existing graphical criteria, leaving the claimed law-restricted identification advantage without a substantive positive example. General separating tables are only real algebraic, while rational replacement and effective height control remain explicitly open. The inference theorem conditions on an externally fixed oracle and quotient class and is a routine finite-dimensional delta-method result, not an end-to-end discovery-and-inference guarantee. The delivered contribution is therefore a narrow exact-decidability framework rather than a field-level causal identification result. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
